question:
Who said the following?

"No society can surely by flourishing and happy, of which the far greater part of the members are poor and miserable."
solution:
The correct answer is __**Adam Smith**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Adam Smith** is often considered the father of modern economics.
 
• He is best known for his influential work, *The Wealth of Nations*, published in 1776.
 
• Smith introduced the idea of the **invisible hand**, which describes the unintended social benefits of individual actions.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the classical free market economic theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Invisible Hand:**

 
 
• The concept of the invisible hand was introduced by Adam Smith in *The Wealth of Nations*.
 
• It refers to the self-regulating nature of the marketplace, where individual self-interest and freedom of production and consumption result in the overall economic well-being of society.
 
 
 
• **Classical Economics:**
 
 
• Classical economics is a school of thought that originated with Adam Smith and is based on the idea that free markets can regulate themselves through the forces of supply and demand.
 
• Other prominent economists in this school include David Ricardo and John Stuart Mill.
 
 
 
• **The Wealth of Nations:**
 
 
• Published in 1776, this work is considered the cornerstone of classical economics.
 
• In it, Adam Smith discusses the division of labor, productivity, and free markets.
 
 
 
• **Poverty and Inequality:**
 
 
• Adam Smith's quote highlights the issue of poverty and inequality, suggesting that a society cannot truly prosper if the majority of its members are suffering.
 
• This idea is a precursor to modern discussions on economic inequality and social justice.
